Decode many messages into a data frame

Source: R/frame.R
proto_decode_df.Rd

Decodes many messages of one type into a data frame, one row per message, built column by column: every message is decoded first, then each column is filled across all of them. A message that fails stops the whole call, and the condition's index says which one.

Usage

proto_decode_df(
  x,
  type,
  pool,
  field = NULL,
  int64 = c("double", "character"),
  enums = c("factor", "integer", "character"),
  defaults = TRUE,
  bytes = c("raw", "base64"),
  max_size = zpb_default_limits()$max_size,
  max_depth = zpb_default_limits()$max_depth,
  max_rows = 1e+07
)

Arguments

x

For proto_decode_df(), a list of raw vectors, one message each; with field, one message as a raw vector, a path or a connection. For proto_read_delimited(), a raw vector, a path or a connection holding a length-delimited stream.

type

The message type's full name, such as "pkg.Message".

pool

A pool from proto_pool() holding type.

field

The name of a repeated message field of type, or NULL.

int64

How 64-bit integer fields become R values: "double" (values beyond 2^53 lose precision, with a zuproto_precision_loss warning) or "character" (exact decimal strings).

enums

How enum fields become R values: "factor", "integer" (the numbers) or "character" (the names). A number the enum does not define is NA with a zuproto_unknown_enum warning, except as an integer.

defaults

Whether unset fields without presence take their defaults (TRUE) or are left out (FALSE).

bytes

How bytes fields become R values: "raw" or "base64" (strings, as protobuf JSON writes them).

max_size

The largest input accepted, in bytes. upb's memory for the decode is capped at four times this.

max_depth

The deepest nesting accepted: how many levels of messages within messages, the top-level message being level 0. A message holding a message holding a message is depth 2. A map entry counts as a level too, as upb counts it, so a message reached through a map is two levels down. At most 1000, so that hostile input cannot exhaust the C stack.

max_rows

The largest number of rows accepted.

Value

A data frame.

Details

With field, the input is one message instead, and the rows are the elements of its repeated message field field. That is how feeds that wrap their records in one message become tables, a GTFS Realtime FeedMessage and its entity field for one.

Columns

FieldColumn
scalar, enum, scalar-like well-known typeatomic vector, as in proto_decode()
byteslist of raw vectors
messagedata frame (a column of the frame)
repeated scalarlist of vectors
repeated messagelist of data frames
maplist of named vectors or lists
Struct, Value, ListValue, Anylist, as in proto_decode()
oneofa column per member, plus <oneof>_case with the member set
extensiona column named [pkg.ext] per extension the pool knows

A field a row does not set is NA (NULL in a list column) when the field tracks presence; otherwise it takes its default, or is NA with defaults = FALSE. A message field that no row sets is an all-NA logical column rather than a data frame, which is also where the columns of a recursive type end. A message type with no fields, such as Empty, is a list column: list() where set, NULL where not. A nested message that is set but has every field unset reads as unset, since its row is all NA.

See also

proto_read_delimited() for length-delimited streams.

Examples

pool <- proto_pool()
# Three FieldDescriptorProto messages, one per row.
msgs <- lapply(c("id", "name", "when"), function(name) {
  proto_encode(list(name = name, number = 1L), "google.protobuf.FieldDescriptorProto", pool)
})
df <- proto_decode_df(msgs, "google.protobuf.FieldDescriptorProto", pool)
df[c("name", "number")]
#>   name number
#> 1   id      1
#> 2 name      1
#> 3 when      1
